title: Convergent Component Atlas and Thematic Token Migration Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a convergent Component Atlas and a pragmatic token migration playbook to harmonize console surface tokens and component variants used across dashboards, rollout rails, and cost insight microcards. The goal is to reduce visual drift between legacy panels and new metric canvases, enable deterministic rollout behaviors (canary, A/B, fallback), and make a low-friction token migration path for engineering (CSS vars + runtime token mapping).

Scope and deliverables:
- Author a Component Atlas Figma file that documents canonical variants for: metric cards, compact/time-series tiles, rollout rails, status pills, density stacks, and cost-sparkline cells. Each component must include accessibility contrast checks and token references.
- Produce a Token Migration Playbook with mapping tables from legacy tokens to new thematic tokens (surface-*, accent-*, intent-*), migration heuristics, and a rollback strategy for controlled rollouts.
- Prototype a lightweight Figma token library and a living specimen page that demonstrates canary vs full rollout visual states and the cost view delta (old vs new).
- Create a developer-facing migration checklist and a sample CSS var mapping PR (referenced in Dependencies).

Design decisions and rationale:
- Thematic tokens (surface, intent, accent, state) are preferred over numeric tokens to reduce cognitive overhead for cross-team authors. Decision trades: this increases token count but improves intent clarity and rollout safety.
- Introduce a small, namespaced density token set (density-compact, density-regular, density-spacious) rather than per-component spacing tokens to reduce combinatorial variants.
- Preserve legacy alias tokens during migration for a minimum of two releases to support enterprise Dedicated customers on older runtime builds.

Prototype artifacts (links):
- Figma atlas (working): https://www.figma.com/file/fake-convergent-atlas/CONSOLE-Atlas-Work
- Playbook (Confluence draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Component+Atlas+and+Token+Migration
- Dev sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/4321 (tokens/migration-sample)

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma atlas contains documented variants for the 8 prioritized components and token references for each layer.
- Playbook includes token mapping table, one rollback scenario, and step-by-step migration checklist validated by ENG and PM.
- A prototype spec is approved by design lead and product for a canary rollout experiment on the Cost Explorer next sprint.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Token sprawl causing inconsistent visuals in older pages. Mitigation: provide automated token linter and backward aliasing; include migration milestone in the engineering sprint plan.
- Risk: Accessibility regressions due to new accents. Mitigation: preflight contrast checks in Figma and a11y gate in PR checklist.

Next steps:
- Complete Figma atlas first pass (Marco) by 2026-02-21.
- Run a 1-hour cross-team sync with ENG and PM to align rollout constraints (Aisha to schedule).
- Hand off playbook to Solutions Eng for feasibility notes and fill in migration PR stub.
